summary: A first-person investigative piece, begun in September 2023, on how weekly Sunday suppers foster togetherness, health, and cultural continuity. The author visits families and interviews a dietitian, psychologist, food historian, chef, and community leader. The piece concludes that Sunday suppers nourish bonds, mental health, and community, and are adapting through healthier recipes and video calls.
one_line: An investigation into Sunday suppers shows how weekly family meals support nutrition, mental health, cultural heritage, and community, even as they adapt to modern life.
key_facts: The author began investigating Sunday suppers in September 2023, looking at nutritional value and mental health benefits.
On October 3, 2023, the author joined the Evans family in Springfield, where matriarch Mary Evans served pot roast, mashed potatoes, and green beans, a meal in her family for over four generations.

Registered dietitian Emily Larson (interviewed September 15, 2023) said families that eat together have more balanced and varied diets, and children eat more fruits, vegetables, and lean proteins and fewer sugary snacks and fast food.
A study published November 1, 2023 by the American Psychological Association found regular family meals linked to lower rates of depression and anxiety and higher self-esteem and life satisfaction.

Psychologist Dr. Thomas Kline (interviewed December 5, 2023) said the predictability of a weekly meal provides security and routine, and the gatherings offer emotional support and build resilience, especially in children.
Food historian Anna Petrov (interviewed November 20, 2023) called food 'a love language' that preserves stories, values, and heritage along with cooking methods.
The Thomas family in Charleston, visited January 15, 2024, blends Cuban and Southern influences in their Sunday suppers.
Chef and food blogger Ben Hanley, met February 10, 2024, was making a vegan, gluten-free version of his grandmother's famous stew, illustrating healthier, more globalized takes on traditional dishes.
Community leader Maria Gonzalez (March 3, 2024) said strong, connected families lead community initiatives, volunteer, and contribute more actively to society.
The Lin family, visited April 10, 2024, uses video calls to include two children away at college in their Sunday suppers.
